title: Cap. III Rat. 10: Valencia, Vasquez, Faustus — election must rest on foresight of works
pass_a_gloss: This argument is pressed by Gregory of Valencia. Vasquez also uses the same argument. Moreover the ancient Pelagians attacked the Catholics with this argument: For so Faustus of Riez, To those predestinated to life prayer will not be necessary; to those appointed to death it will not be able to profit: in these it will be judged superfluous, in those weak; book 1 On free choice chapter 4. What concerning prayer, that concerning all the rest of good works by the same formula of arguing could be concluded, namely that they are superfluous, the antecedent and gratuitous decree of the divine election having been posited. Election therefore is to be posited from foresight of works.
pass_b_english: Gregory of Valencia presses this; Vasquez uses it too. Even the old Pelagians turned it on the Catholics — so Faustus of Riez (De lib. arb. 1.4): for those predestined to life prayer will not be necessary; for those appointed to death it cannot help — superfluous in the one case, powerless in the other. What they say of prayer they could conclude of every other good work: superfluous once an antecedent, gratuitous decree of divine election is posited. Therefore election must be set on foresight of works.
source_text: Hoc argumentum urgetur a Gregorio de Valencia. Vasques etiam eodem argumento utitur. Quinetiam antiqui Pelagiani Catholicos hoc argumento oppugnabant: Sic enim Faustus Regiensis, Praedestinatis ad vitam necessaria non erit oratio; deputatis ad mortem prodesse non poterit: in istis supervacua, in illis infirma judicabitur; lib. 1. De lib. arb. c. 4. Quod de oratione, id de caeteris omnibus bonis operibus eadem argumentandi formula concludi potuit, esse nimirum supervacua, posito antecedente et gratuito decreto electionis Divinae. Electio igitur ponenda ex praescientia operum.
